subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; exact module version needs code/CAD confirmation.
subsystems.intake: Two cantilevered rack-and-pinion cube-intake halves leave a center gap for the arm.
subsystems.transfer: Cross-shaft synchronizes the intake halves; service couplers permit separate removal.
subsystems.scoring: NEO-powered cascading telescope on a chain-driven shoulder; compact printed wrist and roller claw.
subsystems.endgame: Not explained in the retrieved interview.
subsystems.controls: Arm gravity effects require tuning across extension; setup and motion integrated with swerve.

versions: Traffic-cone orienting collector concept was shelved; team focused on station cones. Interview is week zero, not a final-season configuration.
dossier.analysis: The intake gap and telescopic packaging are one integrated decision: moving the arm lower during transit can matter as much as its maximum reach. Shelf loading was an explicit scope reduction.
limits: Interview configuration and reported revisions are documented; full season chronology remains to be audited against the linked releases.

context_documents.title: 2023-125 · Split rack collectors preserve a central arm corridor
context_documents.body:
# 2023-125: Split rack collectors preserve a central arm corridor

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Two cantilevered rack-and-pinion collector halves leave space for a telescoping arm, synchronized by a cross-shaft with service couplers. The shoulder transmission is nested below the arm; a compact wrist and roller claw complete direct scoring.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team identifies robust, controllable deployment and avoiding pneumatics as reasons for the rack choice. Shoulder placement is tied to maximizing useful stowed arm length.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

The center gap is not wasted intake width: it is clearance purchased for another mechanism. Synchronization must keep both collector halves from racking while still permitting fast replacement. As the arm extends, gravity torque rises with lever arm, so tuning only the retracted shoulder does not establish controllability at high reach.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test one-sided collector impacts, service-coupler realignment and shoulder tracking at maximum extension with each game piece.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/fmK7OAET3F4](https://youtu.be/fmK7OAET3F4)

source_reviews.title: NUTRONs 2023 Code and CAD Release
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team's release and follow-up answers.
source_reviews.facts: Split rack collector and its removal, iterative printed arm guides, offline trajectories, and central battery/sideways PDH layout are described.
source_reviews.limitations: Mechanism dimensions beyond the written specifications and the deployed program revision were not audited.

source_reviews.title: Behind the Bumpers | 125 NUTRONs, team replies
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team replies on extension, cable routing and electrical limits.
source_reviews.facts: Arm collapse and available travel, helical cable spool, separate power and CAN slip rings, elastic slack compensation and 30 A limits.
source_reviews.limitations: February weight is a pre-ballast snapshot. August replies describe the hardware but do not date its installation.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Duality combined a long telescoping arm and powered wrist with a chassis packaged around a central battery. The early cube collector was divided across the front so the arm could pass between its two sides. The team eventually removed that collector. The arm's electrical services are part of the mechanism design: as the arm changes length, the extension gearbox pays out or retrieves the harness through a helical drum. That interface lets the wrist and roller retain powered control at either end of the stroke.
source_review.piece_flow: The early ground-cube configuration used a deployed roller ahead of the arm's wrist and claw. The two collector halves left a path for the arm to approach or pass through the front. The release describes automatic selection of cone versus cube scoring position from the most recent intake selection and a toggle between single-station poses. After deletion of the ground intake, the documented hardware retained the wrist and claw for direct piece handling. The exact full set of post-deletion pickup locations and the early collector-to-claw timing were not established from these posts.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The team measured the collapsed arm at 23 inches with 52 inches of additional linear travel available. The stance and base packaging must accommodate a large change in reach. The release documents a side-mounted PDH between center frame bars, front swerve and intake connections on one side and rear swerve and arm on the other. Snap-in printed grommets protect the wires through the frame. The team chose this layout to retain a central battery and low, balanced mass. Its offline trajectory solver incorporated velocity, acceleration, jerk and obstacle constraints for the peg and shelf.

subsystems.name: Arm extension, guides and planning
subsystems.construction: Multi-stage telescope with printed bearing blocks. The final blocks reported by the team were printed on Markforged Onyx Ones. The shoulder and extension are coordinated by offline trajectories.
subsystems.operation: Guide fit is tuned after assembly and powder coating. The team measured play, moved bearing locations in the print and reprinted on the same machine.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team optimized part breakup and fit and wanted to move quickly between poses with obstacle and motion constraints.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: At long extension, small guide gaps can become large wrist errors. Test side load, joint reversal and repeated extension with the assembled coating stack.
subsystems.interfaces: The telescope carries the powered wrist. The extension gearbox also drives harness payout. The early collector shares the arm's swept corridor.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Keep printed spare guides matched to real tube lots and coatings. Recheck clearance and endpoint calibration after installing a replacement.
subsystems.unknowns: Final bearing preload, telescope section sizes, shoulder drive geometry and trajectory deployment by event.

subsystems.name: Wrist, rollers and harness
subsystems.construction: Compact printed wrist and end-effector parts, two NEOs with Spark MAX controllers, a helical cable drum driven from the extension gearbox, and separate four-wire power and CAN slip rings. Surgical tubing tensions an approximately eight-inch cable section.
subsystems.operation: The drum winds or pays out with extension. The elastic section takes up mismatch at direction changes. Wrist and intake circuits each use a 30 A breaker and controller current limit.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team used reduction to make the wrist controllable while holding position and prototyped the roller to preserve adequate acquisition and ejection with the current cap.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A spool phase error accumulates with stroke. The elastic section needs enough travel to absorb reversals without concealing excessive tension at full reach.
subsystems.interfaces: Power and CAN cross the rotating drum boundary. Harness motion is mechanically tied to extension rather than to a separate motor.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check strand condition, slip-ring continuity and voltage at the tip through repeated reversals. Validate that the roller clears a jam under its current limit.
subsystems.unknowns: Slip-ring models, spool ratio, harness fatigue life and roller compression.

subsystems.name: Split collector and base
subsystems.construction: Early roller split across the front. Aluminum and printed rack assemblies ride on printed bearing blocks. The chassis routes front and rear swerve wiring to opposite PDH sides.
subsystems.operation: The deployed roller collects while leaving room for the arm to swing through its center. The later robot dispensed with that intake.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team states the split was for arm clearance. February plans included 26 lb of low steel ballast after a 78 lb pre-ballast weigh-in.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A centered corridor exchanges usable roller width for collision clearance. An offset strike can bind one rack while the other still moves.
subsystems.interfaces: The racks and arm compete for front-frame space. The base distributes arm and ballast loads to the wheels.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check both racks after unilateral impact and reproduce handoff with the real bumpers and held piece before copying the arrangement.
subsystems.unknowns: Collector synchronization hardware in the final early-season revision, the date of removal, and final official weight.

revisions: Ground collector removed during the season. The team reports nearly a dozen telescope bearing-block iterations, including final post-coating fit correction. The February ballast plan and August cable explanation are separately dated reports.
transferable_principles: Design telescoping cable travel with the extension transmission and include a tolerance absorber. Measure printed guide fit after finishing the real assembly.
disconfirming_conditions: A synchronized cable spool offers little benefit if full-stroke electrical reliability is worse than a routed harness. A dedicated intake earns its space only if its acquisition advantage survives transfer and recovery time.
remaining_gaps: Installed event-by-event mechanisms, direct-pickup pose coverage after collector deletion, measured cycle times and endurance of the slip-ring path.
